newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Winterthur defends capital under review.
newsitem.headline: Winterthur defends capital under review.

text.p: Swiss insurer Winterthur defended its capitalisation policy and profit growth after rating agency Moody's put Winterthur under review for a possible downgrade.

Winterthur Insurance Co said in a statement lower capitalisation was a result of immediately writing off goodwill for buying profitable insurers in recent years whose earnings would boost overall group results.

Moody's said on Tuesday it was considering placing the Aaa-rated insurer under review due to matters related to "solvency pressures arising from its acquisition strategy, and the lessening quality of its earnings."
Winterthur said its capital ratios far exceeded European Union capital requirements.
"Winterthur does not believe that a level of capitalisation has to meet the maximal demands of rating agencies," the insurance group said.
"Instead, Winterthur seeks to achieve an optimum between security on one hand and on the other hand the interest of shareholders in adding value and profit per share," it said.
Winterthur noted its half year report in early October had shown a 10 percent increase in shareholder equity in the first six months of 1996, to 4.4 billion Swiss francs from 4.0 billion.
It also noted that half-year net profit jumped 24 percent from a year earlier, to 248.4 million Swiss francs.
Winterthur in October forecast a double-digit percentage increase in net profit for the full year.
Moody's said in a statement released Tuesday that it had placed Winterthur under review for possible downgrade, which would affect approximately $721.1 million of debt securities.
In September, ratings firm Standard & Poor's already lowered its claims-paying ability rating of Winterthur to "AA-minus" from "AAA."

S&P said its reason for the downgrade was belief that "current and prospective capital adequacy is not sufficient for the maintenance of a triple A rating, following two years of acquisition-led growth, together with higher financial and investment leverage and an increasing focus on the group's return on equity in general.
